questions.stem:
Statements: No tokens is a notes. Some notes are loans. All loans are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All tokens are bonds.
II. Some bonds are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few tokens are notes. Some notes are loans. All loans are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All tokens are bonds.
II. No notes is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some tokens are notes. All notes are loans. No loans is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some tokens are loans.
II. Some notes are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few tokens are notes. All notes are loans. No loans is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some tokens are not notes.
II. No notes is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings secure access = pa vo ni
savings banking credit = ka vo mi
secure banking digital = ni mi lu
access credit digital = lu pa ka
savings secure digital = vo ni lu
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = vo, secure = ni, access = pa, banking = mi, credit = ka, digital = lu.

Statements: V = U = S < X > Q.
Conclusions: I. Q ≤ V   II. V ≤ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: B is the brother of C. C is the mother of G. E is the father of B and C. How is B related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of G’s mother C. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the mother of H. E is the son of H. C is the father of H. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. C is a parent of H, and E is H’s son. Hence E is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of C. C is the father of F. A is the son of F. E is the sister of C. How is C related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of F, and F is A’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 112 km north, turns left and walks 216 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 234. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 90 km along the initial direction and 216 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(90² + 216²) = 234 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 66 km west, turns left and walks 56 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 70. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 42 km along the initial direction and 56 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(42² + 56²) = 70 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 51 km north, turns left and walks 75 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 40 km along the initial direction and 75 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(40² + 75²) = 85 km.
